newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-WALES PLAYERS VOTE FOR "BAD GUY" JONES AS CAPTAIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WALES PLAYERS VOTE FOR "BAD GUY" JONES AS CAPTAIN.

text.p: Vinnie Jones, often labelled the villain of British football, was on Friday named captain of Wales by popular demand of his team mates.
Regular skipper Barry Horne is out injured for Saturday's World Cup qualifier against the Netherlands, so Wales manager Bobby Gould let his players choose a replacement for the match in Eindhoven.
They voted for midfielder Jones, who has been sent off 12 times during his stormy career and revels in a "hardman" image.
"He's had more (yellow and red) cards than there are nails in the Moerdijk bridge (south of Rotterdam)," crowed the best-selling newspaper Telegraaf on Thursday.
Gould, anxious to avoid accusations of bias because he was once Jones's manager at English club Wimbledon, said: "We had a democratic vote. The players know who they want to lead them.
"Some people say it's a sad day for football and Vinnie will have to live with that but I have always said he is under-rated."
Jones, 31, who turned to professional football after beginning working life as a hod carrier, said: "It is the proudest day of my career."
He said he would not swap his shirt after the match, which the Netherlands are expected to win comfortably.
They beat Wales 3-1 in Cardiff last month, their fourth successive victory over the Welsh.

Even without Winston Bogarde, Patrick Kluivert, Richard Witschge, John Veldman and Peter Hoekstra of Ajax, as well as experienced defender Stan Valckx and Manchester United's Jordi Cruyff, they look far stronger.
Arsenal's Dennis Bergkamp is recalled and is likely to support Celtic's Pierre van Hooydonk, who as a substitute in Cardiff scored two of the Dutch goals.
Ajax winger Marc Overmars is also back in the squad after an absence of almost a year following knee surgery.
In Ajax's recent 4-1 European Champions' League drubbing of Glasgow Rangers, Overmars looked fit, fast and well on the way to recovering his electric form of the previous two seasons.
Van Hooydonk and defender Frank de Boer have been receiving treatment for minor strains but are expected to play.
